title: deployment-bakeoff-notes-jh
content:
Purpose
Quick personal scratchpad for the deployment bakeoff between two rollout strategies for rdx-serve v2.1 (model + runtime). Trying to pick a default canary cadence and pinning approach that balances latency SLOs and cost. Not for external sharing yet — rough notes.

Context
- Target: hosted inference route /v1/generate using rdx-serve:v2.1 (quantized) + runtime-optimizations on GPU-pool-3.
- Risk: small regressions in token-level latency p95 and occasional 500s from new KV cache edge-case.
- Constraint: Prod traffic peak 3.2k rps, will ramp reserves to handle additional canary load without impacting SLAs.

Two candidate strategies (bakeoff):
A) Micro-increment canary (gradual): 0.1% -> 0.5% -> 1% -> 2% -> 5% -> 10% (30m between steps)
   - Pros: fine-grained, easier to abort early, good for subtle regressions
   - Cons: longer overall window (~3-4h), more operational complexity

B) Short burst canary (fast): 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% (10-15m between steps)
   - Pros: faster validation for heavy-tailed latencies, quicker to reach coverage
   - Cons: bigger blast radius if something wrong, harder to detect slowly-accumulating errors

Things to measure (pass/fail heuristics)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 token latency for canary vs baseline (alert if p95 delta > +15% over 15m)
- Errors: 5xx rate absolute and relative (alert if >0.5% absolute or >2x baseline)
- Cost: ephemeral GPU utilization and token cost; note any spike >10% over baseline
- Quality: quick smoke evals on 50 curated prompts (check hallucination/formatting regressions)
- Downstream: queue depth for batched workers, retry amplification metrics

Preflight checklist (what I need to do personally)
- [ ] Confirm model artifact tag rdx-serve:v2.1 was built from CI run 2147 and passed unit tests (GH PR above).
- [ ] Update route config in staging and run A/B traffic for 24h to collect baseline diffs.
- [ ] Prepare canary cohort: internal testers + synthetic traffic mimic of peak prompts.
- [ ] Create dashboard slice: route=hosted-generate, model=rdx-serve:v2.1, window=5m, group=canary_vs_prod.
- [ ] Slack alert channel #deploy-canary and on-call SRE ping list.
- [ ] Prepare rollback runbooks/commands (quick commands below).

Pinned routing notes (version pinning options)
- Pin at edge-router: route-level pin is safest for client determinism; but requires edge config rollout which can be slower.
- Pin via cookie/assigner: maintain sticky sessions for canary cohort, useful for multi-request flows.
- Session affinity caveat: if tokens are cached, affinity can bias KV cache warmup; consider rotating affinity after warmup period.

Quick rollback and ops commands (to remember)
- Rollback route to stable: redwoodctl routes update --route hosted-generate --model rdx-serve:v2.0
- Force-evict canary pool: redwoodctl capacity drain --pool canary-pool-3 --force
- Pin traffic back to stable: redwoodctl rollout set-split --route hosted-generate --split stable=100,canary=0
- Read logs for a model: redwoodctl logs --model rdx-serve:v2.1 --since 30m | grep ERROR

Smoke eval harness (quick steps)
1) Run smoke script against canary endpoint with curated_prompts_small.json (50 items)
2) Compare outputs to baseline snapshots, fail if >3 diffs that indicate format loss or hallucinations.
3) Push quick eval results into slack via /deploy-report (automation hook).

Observability specifics (what I want on dashboards)
- Per-route: requests/min, p50/p95/p99 token latency, token throughput (tokens/sec), model-inferred batch size distribution.
- Per-instance: GPU util, memory, OOMs, loadavg, kernel retries.
- Traces: 99th percentile trace sampling for canary, with tag model:rdx-serve:v2.1.
- E2E: client perceived latency (edge + runtime) via synthetic agents in three regions.

Open questions / TODOs
- How to capture regression in quality that is subtle (semantic drift) during short canaries? Need a small auto-eval suite with weighted scoring.
- Should we prefer edge pinning or route-level pinning for hosted customers who also use Dedicated? Tradeoffs TBD.
- If we observe small steady error increase (0.1% -> 0.3%) over 2h, what's the automated threshold to auto-fallback? Need guardrails.

Notes to self (less formal)
- Try micro-increment on low-traffic window (02:00-05:00 PT) first for safety.
- If micro-increment is too noisy, fall back to burst canary but keep smoke eval strict.
- Remember to annotate the rollout in the release tracker and link to postmortem doc if anything weird.

Post-rollout observation plan (first 6h)
- 0-15m: watch for immediate 5xx spikes and p99 tails. Abort if >1% 5xx.
- 15-60m: validate latencies/p95 within 15% and smoke eval passes.
- 1-6h: watch for cumulative error increases and any customer-facing incidents.

If this goes well: propose default canary policy for rdx-serve minor releases: micro-increment with 30m steps and mandatory smoke-eval pass before >10% traffic.

Random snippets/scratch commands
- curl -X POST https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d @sample_prompt.json
- small script: scripts/run_smoke_eval.sh --endpoint canary --prompts curated_prompts_small.json

End of notes. Will iterate after staging run.
